q: The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation ut + uuₓ + uₓₓ + uₓₓₓₓ = 0 is important in infinite-dimensional dynamics because:
opts: It has a finite-dimensional global attractor despite being an infinite-dimensional system
exp: The KS equation is a canonical example of a dissipative PDE with chaotic spatiotemporal dynamics. It has a finite-dimensional global attractor and is used to study turbulence, flame propagation, and spatiotemporal chaos.
